docs.presetsComponents.component: An assembly out of several nodes — a component the way this shelf means it, next to the
shapes on `Presets/Bounds` and the records on `Presets/Surfaces`.
`ArrowHead` opens the shelf: one node, one preset shape out of the head registry, one record —
the same kind of thing `rect` and `circle` are for `Bounded`, which is why it moved here rather
than staying an `Atoms/Surfaced` lesson. `Arrow`, after it, is where a head stops standing
alone: a component is a registration away, exactly like a shape or a surface. `arrow()` comes
back as three nodes — the run, and one for each end that has something standing on it. Nothing
new was needed for that. No atom, no field, no sort: it is `Bounded + Surfaced` three times
over, and the run's own half of the picture is `Atoms/Surfaced → Path`.
So the panel here holds three whole records, one per node. A hairline run under a solid point
is two of them disagreeing on purpose; a head carrying a picture is a third. Sewn into the
line's own contour a head would have been stuck with the line's paint, and with being a path
docs.presetsComponents.arrowHead: One end of an arrow, on its own — because that is what it is: one node, one shape, one
The shape comes out of a registry by name. `pointer`, `begin`, `stop` and `diamond` are the
stock four; a fifth is a `registerHead` call with any closed shape at all behind it, which
is why a suit or a piece is not a special case and needs nothing added here.
Unlike a run, THIS shape has an inside — so the fill is doing something, and the same record
can make the head solid, hollow, or a box with a picture on it. That is the whole reason a
head is its own node rather than a detour in the line's contour: one node wears one record,
and an arrow usually wants two.
`turn` is the angle a path arriving at that angle would give it. On its own a head knows
nothing about paths — `Arrow`, below, is where the two meet.
docs.presetsComponents.arrow: One call, and the whole family of them.
A straight run, a bowed one, a swoosh from a drawing tool, an arrow, a double-headed arrow, a
measurement bar: every one of those is this call with different numbers in it. `from` and `to`
are the ends of the run; `bend` bows its middle without moving either; `through` — written in
the code rather than put on a control — names places the path is dragged through, which is how
a curve arrives from a tool that drew it.
`startHead` and `endHead` name a head out of the registry, each with its own size and its own
record. Clear one and that node is not there at all: an end with nothing on it is the ordinary
case, not an empty box. A fifth head is a `registerHead` call with any closed shape behind it —
a suit, a piece — and an unknown name draws nothing rather than throwing.
What is NOT here, deliberately: anything that walks the path over time. Footprints laid along a
route, a run that draws itself on arrival, a silhouette traced round a contour — those are a
mechanic of their own, and keeping them out is what leaves this one simple enough to build them
